how_we_lost: P1 (Teval lands) won on round 8. Its landfall engine (Field of the Dead, The Gitrog Monster, Tatyova, Cauldron of Essence, Timeless Witness, Teval returning lands) went off on T29. Ob Nixilis, the Fallen's landfall drained P2 out and grew to 27/27, and the Zombie swarm killed P3. On T32 P1 aimed 4 landfall drains at us (12) and attacked with about 20 creatures (33 combat damage), which was lethal from 35. Nobody touched us until round 8, but Muldrotha only arrived on T31 (round 8). Our one attempt at Ob Nixilis, Galactus chapter I on T28, was countered by An Offer You Can't Refuse.
winnable_why: We had seven quiet rounds, but we were slow: a 1-land 8-card keep, missed land drops, a land sacrificed, and Talisman held for 4 turns. By round 8 P1 had about 70 power of black creatures and tokens. Our in-hand answers (Invasion, Shriekmaw, Capsule, Plaguecrafter) can't handle that, and only a sweeper would (Massacre Wurm, Pernicious Deed, Ratchet Bomb at 0, Toxic Deluge), none of which we drew. Killing Ob Nixilis at 3/3 on T24 and ramping on time would have slowed P1 a lot and kept P2 and P3 alive as buffers, but winning still needed a sweeper.

mistakes.what_happened: Round 6. The memo named P1's newly cast Ob Nixilis, the Fallen (3/3) as threat #1, answered by Invasion of Innistrad or Galactus I. The memo's actual line was Talisman plus casting Hearthhull from Hostage Taker's exile. The executor accepted Forge's cast of Vrock with all 5 mana. The memo had said to hold Vrock until Muldrotha.
mistakes.better_play: Talisman of Dominance (2), then Invasion of Innistrad (4) on Ob Nixilis: exactly 5 sources plus Talisman.
mistakes.why: Ob Nixilis became the 27/27 that drained P2 to death on T29 (six triggers) and hit us for 12 on the lethal turn. At 3/3, before its first landfall, it dies to anything.
mistakes.category: no removal on the real threat

mistakes.what_happened: Round 3. We had 3 lands on the battlefield and none in hand. The executor OVERRULED Forge's 'hold' to sacrifice Nurturing Peatland to draw a card. Talisman of Dominance, which the memo said to cast first, stayed in hand. We started round 4 on 2 lands and round 5 on 3.
mistakes.better_play: Keep Peatland. Cast Talisman plus Baleful Strix as the memo said.
mistakes.why: Muldrotha needs 6 sources. Sacrificing a land when land-light is the most expensive card draw in the deck. Together with the next item, it pushed Muldrotha from about round 5-6 to round 8, the turn after P1's explosion.

mistakes.what_happened: Talisman of Dominance sat in hand from T4 to T28, although the memos on T12, T16, T20 and T24 each said to cast it. The mana went to Strix plus the Peatland draw (T12), Capsule cast and cracked (T16), Hostage Taker (T20) and Vrock (T24). On T20 the memo's line (Talisman plus Mind Stone, Muldrotha next turn on 6 sources) was replaced by Hostage Taker on a 2-counter Hearthhull. Hearthhull is P2's commander, so it went back to the command zone and was recast on T30.
mistakes.better_play: Talisman on T12, and Talisman plus Mind Stone on T20, then Muldrotha on T24 with Capsule recursion online.
mistakes.why: Muldrotha arrived 2 rounds late, the turn after P1 went off. Hostage Taker on a commander is only a tempo bounce.

mistakes.what_happened: We kept 8 cards on the draw with 1 land (Marsh Flats) plus Birds, Farseek and Talisman, and missed land drops on rounds 2 and 5.
mistakes.better_play: Borderline. Keeping is defensible with Birds + Farseek + Talisman, but the hand needed a land by turn 3 to cast Muldrotha on time. A 7 with 3 lands is safer for a 6-drop commander deck.
mistakes.why: It contributed to the late Muldrotha, though less than the Peatland sacrifice and the held Talisman.

strategy_assessment: The memos' threat model was pointed at the wrong opponent for most of the game. They earmarked Galactus and Hostage Taker for P2's Hearthhull, spent Capsule on P3's Righteous Valkyrie, and repeatedly deferred ramp, while P1's Teval landfall deck assembled Field of the Dead, Gitrog, Tatyova, Cauldron and Ob Nixilis. The strategist did flag Ob Nixilis on T24, but the answer was never cast. Against this table the plan should have been: (1) cast the rocks on curve and get Muldrotha down by round 5-6; (2) kill landfall payoffs (Ob Nixilis, Gitrog, Tatyova) on sight, because the Teval deck converts every land into damage or bodies; (3) tutor (Demonic Tutor, Survival) toward a token sweeper (Massacre Wurm, Ratchet Bomb at 0, Pernicious Deed), since P1's win is a wide black token army that our spot removal can't touch (Capsule and Shriekmaw can't hit black creatures). The executor again replaced memo lines with Forge's plays (Vrock on T24, Hostage Taker on T20) and made its own bad overrule (the Peatland sacrifice).
summary: We were never attacked for seven rounds but developed too slowly: a 1-land keep, Peatland sacrificed while land-light, Talisman held for 4 turns. Muldrotha landed the turn after P1's Teval/Field of the Dead/Ob Nixilis engine went off and killed the table. The key miss was T24: Vrock instead of Talisman plus Invasion of Innistrad on a 3/3 Ob Nixilis. Even so, winning needed a sweeper we never drew.
